arxiv-1712-05722.title: Radiative Seesaw Model and DAMPE Excess from Leptophilic Gauge Symmetry
arxiv-1712-05722.creator: Zhi-Long Han 1, Weijian Wang 2, Ran Ding 3
arxiv-1712-05722.description: Abstract In the light of the e + + e − e^{+}+e^{-} excess observed by DAMPE experiment, we propose an anomaly-free radiative seesaw model with an alternative leptophilic U ​ ( 1 ) X U(1)_{X} gauge symmetry. In the model, only right-handed leptons are charged under U ​ ( 1 ) X U(1)_{X} symmetry.

arxiv-2208-08225.title: On the Role of Negative Precedent in Legal Outcome Prediction
arxiv-2208-08225.creator: Josef Valvoda, Ryan Cotterell, Simone Teufel
arxiv-2208-08225.description: Abstract Every legal case sets a precedent by developing the law in one of the following two ways. It either expands its scope, in which case it sets positive precedent, or it narrows it, in which case it sets negative precedent. Legal outcome prediction, the prediction of positive outcome, is an increasingly popular task in AI.

arxiv-2301-06520.title: UL-DL Duality for Cell-free Massive MIMO with Per-AP Power and Information Constraints Thanks: L. Miretti and S. Stańczak are with the Network Information Theory group, Technische Universität Berlin, Berlin 10587, Germany, and the Department of Wireless Communications and Networks, Fraunhofer Instit
arxiv-2301-06520.creator: Lorenzo Miretti, Renato L. G. Cavalcante, Emil Björnson, Sławomir Stańczak
arxiv-2301-06520.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Lorenzo Miretti, Renato L. G. Cavalcante, Emil Björnson, Sławomir Stańczak. We derive a novel uplink-downlink duality principle for optimal joint precoding design under per-transmitter power and information constraints in fading channels. The information constraints model limited sharing of channel state information and data bearing signals across the transmitters. The main application is to cell-free networks, where each access point (AP) must typically satisfy an individual power constraint and form its transmit signal using limited cooperation capabilities.

arxiv-2406-03695.title: FACOS: Enabling Privacy Protection Through Fine-Grained Access Control with On-chain and Off-chain System
arxiv-2406-03695.creator: Chao Liu, Cankun Hou, Tianyu Jiang, Jianting Ning, Hui Qiao, Yusen Wu
arxiv-2406-03695.description: Abstract Data-driven landscape across finance, government, and healthcare, the continuous generation of information demands robust solutions for secure storage, efficient dissemination, and fine-grained access control. Blockchain technology emerges as a significant tool, offering decentralized storage while upholding the tenets of data security and accessibility.

arxiv-2409-10362.title: Frequency-Guided Masking for Enhanced Vision Self-Supervised Learning
arxiv-2409-10362.creator: Amin Karimi Monsefi, Mengxi Zhou, Nastaran Karimi Monsefi, Ser-Nam Lim, Wei-Lun Chao, Rajiv Ramnath {karimimonsefi.1, chao.209, ramnath.6}@osu.edu , sernam@ucf.edu
arxiv-2409-10362.description: Abstract We present a novel frequency-based Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) approach that significantly enhances its efficacy for pre-training. Prior work in this direction masks out pre-defined frequencies in the input image and employs a reconstruction loss to pre-train the model. While achieving promising results, such an implementation has two fundamental limitations as identified in our paper.

arxiv-2411-15432.title: Lifelong Knowledge Editing for Vision Language Models with Low-Rank Mixture-of-Experts
arxiv-2411-15432.creator: Qizhou Chen, Chengyu Wang, Dakan Wang, Taolin Zhang, Wangyue Li, Xiaofeng He
arxiv-2411-15432.description: Abstract Model editing aims to correct inaccurate knowledge, update outdated information, and incorporate new data into Large Language Models (LLMs) without the need for retraining. This task poses challenges in lifelong scenarios where edits must be continuously applied for real-world applications.

arxiv-2507-02414.title: Privacy-preserving Preselection for Face Identification Based on Packing
arxiv-2507-02414.creator: Rundong Xin, Taotao Wang, Jin Wang, Chonghe Zhao, Jing Wang 🖂
arxiv-2507-02414.description: Abstract Face identification systems operating in the ciphertext domain have garnered significant attention due to increasing privacy concerns and the potential recovery of original facial data. However, as the size of ciphertext template libraries grows, the face retrieval process becomes progressively more time-intensive.

pmc-10617706.title: Characterisation of physicochemical parameters and antibacterial properties of New Caledonian honeys
pmc-10617706.creator: Marcela Bucekova, Jana Godocikova, Romain Gueyte, Céline Chambrey, Juraj Majtan, Filippo Giarratana, Filippo Giarratana, Filippo Giarratana
pmc-10617706.description: Honey is an attractive natural product with various health benefits. A few honey-based commercial products have successfully been adopted in clinics to improve wound healing. However, screening of other potential sources of medical-grade honey, in particular, honeys from territories with high floral species diversity and high endemicity, is highly needed.

pmc-10709845.title: Randomised controlled trial of neurostimulation for symptoms of anorexia nervosa (TRENA study): study protocol
pmc-10709845.creator: Anna J Harvey, Sloane Madden, Anthony Rodgers, Michael Bull, Mary Lou Chatterton, Dusan Hadzi-Pavlovic, Colleen K Loo, Donel M Martin
pmc-10709845.description: BackgroundAnorexia nervosa (AN) has amongst the highest mortality rates and the highest treatment costs of any psychiatric disorder. Recently, interest in non-invasive brain stimulation as a novel treatment for AN has grown. These include repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS).

pmc-10774773.title: Molecular evolution, virology and spatial distribution of HCV genotypes in Pakistan: A meta-analysis
pmc-10774773.creator: Arslan Habib, Nadiya Habib, Khalid Mahmood Anjum, Riffat Iqbal, Zeeshan Ashraf, Muhammad Usman Taj, Muhammad Asim, Kanwal Javid, Faezeh Idoon, Saeid Dashti, Cassio Rocha Medeiros, Ana Pavla Almeida Diniz Gurgel, Henrique Douglas Melo Coutinho
pmc-10774773.description: Highlights•Genotype 3 of hepatitis C virus (HCV) is the most prevalent genotype in Pakistan.•Estimation of genotype is a productive method to help in the duration and selection of antiviral treatment.•Different factors are a barrier in the way to reduce the prevalence of HCV in Pakistan.

pmc-11437255.title: Permeability monitoring of underground concrete structures using elastic wave characteristics with modified Biot’s model
pmc-11437255.creator: Jong-Won Lee, Jin-Seop Kim, Chang-Ho Hong, Tae-Min Oh
pmc-11437255.description: This study aims to develop a theoretical model for predicting the permeability of concrete in underground structures using compressive elastic waves. This research is motivated by the necessity of monitoring the permeability of concrete used in critical underground infrastructure, such as tunnels and radioactive waste disposal sites, to ensure their long-term safety.

pmc-11550949.title: Accelerated innervation of biofabricated skeletal muscle implants containing a neurotrophic factor delivery system
pmc-11550949.creator: Vladimir Mashanov, Erika Billman, Aurelia Poerio, Mary Kaufmann, Dehui Lai, J. William Vaughan, Ickhee Kim, Young Min Ju, Anthony Atala, James J. Yoo, Ji Hyun Kim
pmc-11550949.description: IntroductionVolumetric muscle loss (VML) is one of the most severe and debilitating conditions in orthopedic and regenerative medicine. Current treatment modalities often fail to restore the normal structure and function of the damaged skeletal muscle. Bioengineered tissue constructs using the patient’s own cells have emerged as a promising alternative treatment option, showing positive outcomes in fostering new muscle tissue formation.

pmc-11580247.title: Gender differences in burnout among US nurse leaders during COVID-19 pandemic: an online cross-sectional survey study
pmc-11580247.creator: Latifah Alenezi, Gordon Lee Gillespie, Carolyn Smith, Kermit G Davis
pmc-11580247.description: AbstractObjectivesAmong nurse leaders, gender should receive particular attention, because life and work experiences and burnout during COVID-19 pandemic may vary between women and men, potentially requiring different strategies to achieve well-being. Thus, information about gender differences in burnout might be critical to burnout prevention in nurse leaders.

pmc-11692533.title: REFRAMING AGING: THROUGH THE LENS OF ETHICAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
pmc-11692533.creator: Cynthia McNellis
pmc-11692533.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology is advancing at a rapid pace. In addition, our older adult cohort is growing at an unprecedented rate. The purpose of my research is to address the ethical concerns when AI intersects with this population, offering policy recommendations to bridge this ethical digital divide.

pmc-12703416.title: Ball‐Milling Assisted Iron‐Catalyzed Difluoromethylation Toward the Synthesis of Valuable Oxindoles
pmc-12703416.creator: Vitalii Solomin, Nicolas Delcroix, Marie Caldiero, Philippe Jubault, Thomas Castanheiro
pmc-12703416.description: SEM analyses revealed that the ball‐milling and piezoelectric‐mediated radical difluoromethylation might be, in fact, catalyzed by iron contamination of BaTiO3 due to abrasion of the stainless steel milling assembly (jar and balls). A ball‐milling mediated, Fe‐catalyzed radical difluoromethylation is subsequently developed for the synthesis of valuable difluoromethylated oxindoles.

pmc-13417314.title: Meniscus Tissue Engineering Scaffolds: Biomaterials, Biofabrication, and Translation
pmc-13417314.creator: Wenbo Jin, Wenyu Ning, Ruoyu Wang, Danyang Zhao, Liangkun Lu, Fei Duan, Jian Yang, Cheng Zhang, Kedong Song
pmc-13417314.description: The meniscus is a fibrocartilaginous tissue essential for load transmission, shock absorption, joint stability, and cartilage protection in the knee. However, its intrinsic healing capacity is severely limited, particularly in the avascular region and in complex defects, often resulting in persistent symptoms, functional impairment, and progressive joint degeneration.

pmc-13591816.title: Clinical characteristics and an admission-time predictive model for severe scrub typhus and secondary HLH in adults
pmc-13591816.creator: Changqi Guo, Xin Zhang, Chonghuan Li, Yibin Huang, Jiawei Su, Yijing Wang, Chao Zhuo, Ling Yang
pmc-13591816.description: BackgroundScrub typhus can rapidly progress to severe disease with multi-organ dysfunction. Secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is an increasingly recognized hyperinflammatory complication associated with high mortality, but adult data and simple admission-time risk tools remain limited.MethodsWe conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of hospitalized adults with scrub typhus at the First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University (May 2013–July 2025).
